prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: hire a California personal-injury attorney (auto-accident specialist) with experience handling Alameda County/Contra Costa cases, who takes cases on contingency, has trial experience (if your case might not settle), and with whom you feel comfortable communicating. I can help find specific names if you want — tell me whether there were serious injuries, fatalities, or major property damage and whether an insurance company already contacted you.

Below are practical steps and what to look for when choosing a lawyer in Pleasanton (or nearby cities):

1. Type of lawyer
- Look for a personal injury attorney who focuses on car/auto collisions. If your case involves catastrophic injury or wrongful death, find someone who regularly handles those higher-value catastrophic cases.

2. Where to look
- Alameda County Bar Association lawyer referral
- California State Bar website (to confirm license and discipline history)
- Local firm websites, Google/Yelp reviews, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell
- Recommendations from friends/family if available

3. What matters most
- Relevant experience: number of auto-accident cases and verdicts/settlements in CA/Alameda County
- Trial experience: most cases settle, but you want an attorney willing to go to court if needed
- Contingency-fee handling and how they handle costs (who advances expenses)
- Clear communication and regular updates
- A supportive team (paralegals, medical liaison) to manage documents and treatment
- Track record with the insurance companies involved

4. Questions to ask in a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many settled vs. taken to trial?
- Have you handled cases against [name of insurer] before?
- Who will handle the file day to day — you or a paralegal/associate?
- What is your contingency fee and how are costs handled/deducted?
- What is your estimate of my case value and why? (ask them to explain assumptions)
- How long do you expect this to take?
- Can you provide references or examples of similar cases you resolved?

5. Typical fees and costs
- Contingency fees in CA commonly range about 25–40% depending on whether suit is filed and complexity. Confirm the exact percentage and whether it changes after filing suit.
- You are generally not billed hourly; the lawyer advances case costs (medical records, filing fees) and recoups them from the recovery.
- Get the fee agreement in writing and read the expenses section carefully.

6. Important immediate steps to protect your case
- Seek and follow medical treatment — document everything.
- Preserve evidence: photos of the scene, vehicle damage, your injuries, and get the police report number.
- Get witness contact info.
- Do not sign releases or accept a full-and-final settlement from an insurer before talking to an attorney.
- Keep records of medical bills, lost wages, repair receipts and correspondence with insurers.

7. Deadlines
- California statute of limitations for personal injury is generally 2 years from the date of injury. Claims against a government entity have much shorter deadlines (often 6 months). Don’t delay contacting a lawyer.

8. How I can help now
- If you want, tell me: date of accident, severity of injuries, whether the police report exists, insurer names, any offers already made. I can then:
  - Shortlist several experienced Pleasanton / Alameda County attorneys or firms,
  - Provide contact details and a short comparison,
  - Suggest specific questions tailored to your situation for consultations.

Would you like me to find specific attorney names and contact info for Pleasanton-area personal injury lawyers? If yes, share a few case details (severity, time since accident, insurer involvement).
